filter.categoriesHelp: The beatmap’s state on osu!. Ranked covers both ranked and approved, as osu! does. Never submitted is a beatmap that exists only on this machine.
filter.dateAddedHelp: When the beatmap arrived on this machine, taken from when osu! created the file. A beatmap imported from osu!stable is dated when it was imported, not when it was made.
filter.dateRankedHelp: When the beatmap was ranked, approved or loved. Only those three ever have a date; everything else is covered by the box above.
filter.dateSubmittedHelp: When the beatmap was first uploaded to osu!. osu! only records this for beatmaps it has ranked, approved or loved; the box above covers every other beatmap.
filter.difficultyHelp: The star rating of the play as it happened, mods included -- so a 5.50★ beatmap played with Double Time is judged at its Double Time rating. osu!’s own calculator produces it. Drag the right handle in from the end to set a ceiling; the far end is no ceiling at all.
filter.includeNeverRanked: Include beatmaps that were never ranked, qualified or loved
filter.includeNoSubmitDate: Include beatmaps with no submission date on record
filter.keywordsHelp: Matched against the song title, the artist, the difficulty name and the mapper. Separate several with commas -- a play counts if any one of them appears anywhere in those four. Leave it empty to accept every beatmap.
filter.lengthHelp: How long the beatmap runs at the speed it was played, so Double Time shortens it. Type either 3:30 or a number of seconds.
filter.menuOff: Choose which plays are recorded at all
filter.menuOn: A filter is on: some plays are not being recorded
filter.modAndNoMods: A mod is required alongside "no mods at all", so no play can be tracked.
filter.modeHelp: The mode the play was set in. A play on a converted beatmap counts as the mode it was played in -- except an unfinished one, which osu! only records the beatmap for, so it counts as the beatmap's own mode.
filter.modsHelp: Click a mod to cycle it: may be used, then must be used, then must not be used. Everything starts at "may be used", so no mod combination is excluded until you say so. Only which mods were on is compared, never how they were configured, and osu!stable plays are matched on what the player actually chose -- osu! adds Classic to them afterwards, which is not a choice anyone made. Autoplay and Cinema are not listed: nothing in this app can ever count them.
filter.needsLazer: Not available here: this needs osu!lazer’s beatmap database, and only osu!stable was found, so this criterion is left wide open.
filter.noCategoryTicked: No category is ticked, so no play can be tracked.
filter.noModeTicked: No mode is ticked, so no play can be tracked.
filter.partNoneOf: use none of the {n} mods marked out
filter.readoutContradiction: Nothing can match. "No mods at all" and {mods} cannot both be true.
filter.readoutNoMods: Tracks plays with no mods at all.
filter.resetDone: Every criterion is wide open again. Save to keep it that way.

filter.savedOn: Play tracking filter saved - it applies to plays from now on
filter.sessionCountMany: {n} plays have not been recorded since the app started because of this filter.

filterModal.offByDefaultAndEvery: Off by default, and every play is tracked. Turning it on changes nothing on its own: every criterion below starts wide open.
filterModal.twoCriteriaCannotJudgeA: Two criteria cannot judge a play that was quit, failed or retried: osu!lazer records no mods and no star rating for a play it discards, so those plays are matched on the other seven. That is deliberate - osu! counts them, so this does.

setting.asIfModOff: as if the mod were off
setting.countUnsubmitted: Count plays osu! could not submit
setting.countUnsubmittedHint: Quits, fails and retries while osu! was offline or signed out, read from osu!lazer’s own log. osu! never received these, so they count here by default - toward your play count, monthly play counts, Most Played, Recent Plays and Total Play Time. Turn this off to match exactly what your osu! profile shows. They are recorded either way
setting.importWhileClosed: Import plays set while the app was closed
setting.importWhileClosedHint: Off by default. Closing the app is how you stop tracking, so a launch normally brings in nothing from the time it was shut. Turn this on and each launch imports what was played while it was closed - back to when it last ran, never further, and never past this profile's own start. The play tracking filter still applies, and Options → Import past plays is still there for one evening at a time.
setting.noStatusSource: No osu!lazer installation was found, and osu!stable does not record a beatmap’s status, so every beatmap already counts and these have no effect.
setting.priceRelaxHint: Relax and Autopilot only. "As if the mod were off" makes relax count as nomod and relax + DT count as DT, which is usually what people mean - but it flatters the score, because a relax run reaches accuracy and combo the player could not by hand. Both numbers come from osu! itself and both are stored, so switching is instant.
setting.savedRejected: Saved - {fields} was not valid and was cleared
setting.unfinishedPlaysHint: Plays that were started but never finished - quit, retried, or failed. The ones osu! counted always count toward your play count, monthly play counts and Most Played, because osu! counts them too; this only decides whether they are listed here. There is no score to show for them: osu!lazer saves a replay only for a map played to the end.
setting.unrankedMapsHint: None by default. These are separate choices because they are not the same thing: a Loved map is played competitively, a graveyarded one may be a draft nobody finished, and a never-submitted one exists only on your machine. pp still comes from osu!, which will happily price any beatmap it is given.
setting.unrankedModsHint: Count plays osu! refuses to rank because of their mods - Relax, Autopilot, or a customised rate such as DT at 1.45x. Off by default: with this on, the profile is no longer comparable with a real osu! account.
setting.warnIncomparable: Warn when scoring is not comparable
setting.warnIncomparableHint: Shows a line in Scores when a setting has made this profile’s pp incomparable with a real osu! account. Turning it off hides that sentence only - the affected scores keep their *. This is also what the note’s "Don’t show again" sets.

sharedSection.onByDefaultOneList: On by default: one list, shared by every profile. Turn it off and each profile keeps its own copy of the list as it stands; turn it back on and the lists are merged. Nothing is lost either way.
shareModal.backUpEverythingHint: Every profile, with its scores, pictures and me! images, as one .zip file. Restore it below, on this computer or another.
shareModal.dataFolderHint: Everything is kept in this one folder. With the app closed, copying it somewhere else is a complete backup too, and putting it back restores it.
shareModal.exportScoresHint: Every score with its beatmap, plus the totals and rank, for a spreadsheet or another tool. It cannot be restored from: Back up is for that.
shareModal.restoreHint: Replaces every profile here with the backup's. Nothing is deleted: what is here now is moved to a before-restore folder inside the data folder.
shareModal.thisPageAsOneHtml: This page as one .html file that works like it: show more, the mode tabs, View Details and the medals all respond. It opens anywhere without this app, nothing in it can change the profile, and it holds nothing about this computer, so it can be put online as it is.
mcosuNote.text: Playing on McOsu? McOsu saves a play only when you finish and pass it, and that is when it reaches this page. Plays you quit, failed or retried are not counted at all: McOsu keeps no record of them. The pp shown here is osu!'s own, from its current pp system, so it can differ from McOsu's.
stableNote.text: Playing on osu!stable? A score reaches this page when you leave the results screen and go back to song select -- that is when stable writes the replay. Plays you quit, failed or retried are not counted at all: stable keeps no record of them. osu!lazer has neither limitation.

updateModal.yourTrackedScoresSettingsAnd: Your tracked scores, settings and profile pictures are kept - they live in data/, which an update never touches. The files being replaced are set aside until the new version is in place, so an update that is interrupted can be undone rather than leaving a half-installed app.
